title: Data Parallelism & Sharding
description: Study ddp and gradient collectives, gradient buckets and overlap, zero stages and state ownership, and fully sharded training lifecycle. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: DDP and gradient collectives
lessons.description: Draw the collective sequence for two ranks and mark a mismatched branch.
lessons.conceptOverview: Data parallel ranks process different data with replicated model state and combine gradients. All ranks must execute compatible collectives; divergent control flow can hang synchronization. Data sampling and loss weighting determine whether the combined update matches the intended objective.
lessons.whyItMatters: Collective participation and ordering must agree across ranks.

lessons.title: Gradient buckets and overlap
lessons.description: Inspect a hypothetical backward timeline and identify which communications could overlap remaining compute.
lessons.conceptOverview: Gradient communication can overlap backward computation when gradients become ready in groups. Bucket sizing trades launch overhead against the opportunity to start communication early. Model structure and network bandwidth influence the useful configuration; tuning needs a timeline profile.
lessons.whyItMatters: Tune overlap from readiness and communication timelines.

lessons.title: ZeRO stages and state ownership
lessons.description: Make a table of optimizer, gradient, and parameter ownership for three ZeRO stages.
lessons.conceptOverview: ZeRO stages progressively partition optimizer state, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel workers. Higher stages reduce replicated state but require more state movement and coordination. Identify exactly which components are partitioned before estimating per-rank memory.
lessons.whyItMatters: Higher ZeRO stages partition additional model-state components.

lessons.title: Fully sharded training lifecycle
lessons.description: Sketch parameter ownership before, during, and after a sharded block's forward pass.
lessons.conceptOverview: Fully sharded approaches materialize needed parameters around computation and reshard state afterward. Peak memory depends on gathered units, prefetching, activations, and optimizer state, not just average shard size. Wrapping boundaries affect both memory and communication.
lessons.whyItMatters: Account for temporary gathered parameters when estimating peak memory.
